name: Astra mart kit cell 0 (r0 c0)
label: monster_overworld/astra-mart-kit-0 (칸 2240)
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

surfaces.part: top frame band of the corner cell
light blue horizontal band with shaded lower edge

answer.evidence: This is the top-left corner cell of a larger kit, 15 px wide by 16 rows, with a rounded corner at rows 0-2 (widths 12, 13, 14, then 15). Column x=8 shows a 1-row outline at row 0, then a light blue band at rows 1-2, a shade at row 3 and a dark line at row 4. Rows 5-8 are a flat purple panel. The pattern then repeats: light blue at rows 9-10, shade at row 11, a darker row 12, and light blue at rows 13-15. The light blue top band is only 2 rows, so it is a frame strip, not a sloped roof or a horizontal surface. The dark row 4 reads as the shadow of that frame, and the band and panel have the same flat tone. The bands at rows 9-10 and 13-15 are also vertical frame strips. No roof slope, ellipse or visible contents appear in this cell, so it reads as a flat front-facing panel with only a rim-like top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny purple block about one tile in size. It is not a whole building with a roof, walls and a door or windows, so it does not match the reference kind. It shows roughly 3 lightness steps against about 6 per material on the references. Its measured 6 visible tones per tile are well below the references' 12 and 10. Near-flat coverage is 0%, but by eye the surface reads as simple banded fills with no tile scallops, plaster speckle or grain. The outline is a dark edge with little material tint, so it reads as a sticker-like line rather than a dark tone of the adjacent material. The 0% near-neutral share of dark edge pixels shows the edge does carry some tint, but the piece is too small and shallow to count as a dark material tone. Overall it is far thinner than the roof, timber and stone detail on the references.

surfaces.part: roof/awning tile plane (top-left corner cell of a larger kit)

answer.evidence: The cell is a corner tile of a larger structure. The column scans show repeating horizontal bands: light blue rows 1-3, a dark line at row 4, purple rows 5-8, light blue rows 9-11, a dark line at row 12, then blue rows 13-15. This reads as sloped roof or awning tile courses with edge lines. The silhouette widens from 12 to 15 over rows 0-3, which is a rounded top-left corner. No wall, door or other vertical south face of 3+ rows is drawn in this cell, so it has a top plane but no front face. It most likely depends on neighbouring cells for the front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny purple block of about 28x32 px, roughly one tile. It is not a whole building with roof, walls and door/windows, so it does not match the reference kind. Measured facts: 6 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and 6 distinct colours in total against 185 and 66. Shading is shallow, at about 2-3 steps of purple with a darker edge, where the references have about 6 steps per material, with per-tile roof highlights, plaster speckle and stone-by-stone shading. The 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral edge pixels come from the small size and a tinted edge, not from real texture. By eye, the interior shows little grain and no roof scallops or wall texture. It looks like a flat sticker next to the richly textured references.

surfaces.part: roof tile slope (top-left corner cell of a mart roof)

answer.evidence: The whole 16x16 cell is a roof plane with repeating tile stripes. Rows 1-2 are light blue, row 3 is a mid edge line, row 4 is dark, rows 5-8 are purple, rows 9-10 are light blue, row 11 is a mid edge line, row 12 is dark, and rows 13-15 are blue. The silhouette widens from 12 to 15 px over rows 0-3, which gives a bevelled top-left corner. The silhouette has no eave-to-wall transition, door, wall or other vertical south face in the cell, so I count 0 front-face rows. The tile bands repeat with no vertical face to end the slope. This looks like a corner fragment of a larger roof, so the front wall would be in other cells of the kit.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny purple icon about one tile in size, with no roof, walls, door or windows. It does not read as a whole building, so it is not the same kind as the references. It has 6 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references. Its near-flat coverage is 0%, but that is only because the piece is so small. The dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), which points to a purple-toned outline, yet the shape is a simple block with a few stripes. It shows roughly 3 lightness steps and no tile scallops, plaster speckle, stone-by-stone shading or grain. Next to the references' multi-step tiled roofs, timber framing and individually shaded stones, it looks much thinner and more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: roof/awning tile courses (top-left corner cell of the kit)

answer.evidence: The cell is a corner tile of a larger kit. The silhouette widens from 12 to 15 px over rows 0-3, which is a rounded corner. After that it is 15 px wide through row 15. The column scans show repeating roof courses. Rows 1-2 are a light-blue edge band, row 3 is shadow, row 4 is dark, and rows 5-8 are the purple body. Rows 9-10 are the next light-blue edge band, row 11 is shadow, row 12 is dark, and rows 13-15 start a third course. This is a sloped tile plane (evidence c) with edge lines and eave shadows. The whole 15-row cell is roof surface. No vertical south face of 3 or more rows is drawn here. The lighter strip at the left is a border, not a receding side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny purple block of about 14x16 px, roughly one tile. It is not a whole building with roof, walls and door/windows, so it does not match the kind of the references. It has only 6 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and it shows a few horizontal slat lines but no roof tile scallops, plaster speckle or stone-by-stone shading. Its dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline reads as a dark purple material tone. The measured 0% near-flat coverage comes from the stripe lines, but the piece carries far less information than either reference, with about 3 shading steps against 5-6. As a building it is much shallower and fails.
